description.narrative:
All 11 members of the Dutch SRHR Alliance contribute significant value to the partnership through governance, programme implementation, learning, and knowledge exchange. Key organizations including Amref, Oxfam Novib, and Wemos provide central management roles, while Hivos, Rutgers, Liliane Fonds, Amref, and Plan International support country-level coordination and mentorship. Choice plays a leading role in strengthening Meaningful and Inclusive Youth Participation across the Alliance’s governance structures.
In addition, organizations such as CoC, VSO, and Aidsfonds contribute technical expertise through participation in knowledge exchange meetings,learning sessions, and collaborative activities coordinated by the Alliance Hub. The partnership emphasizes shared learning, innovation, and cross-country collaboration to strengthenprogramme effectiveness and long-term sustainability. At the global level, the Alliance operates through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), while governance modalities will be further refined during the inception phase. Currently, the Directors’ Meeting—comprising representatives from all 11 organizations—serves as the principal decision-making body for global planning andbudgeting. Decisions are made through consensus whenever possible, or by a two-thirds majority vote when required.

participating-org.narrative:
Hivos was established in 1968, and is an international development organisation guided by humanist values. Together with local civil society organisations in developing countries, Hivos wants to contribute to a free, fair and sustainable world. A world in which all citizens – both women and men – have equal access to opportunities and resources for development and can participate actively andequally in decision-making processes that determine their lives, their society and their future.
Hivos trusts in the creativity and capacity of people. Quality, cooperation and innovation are core values in Hivos’ programme development and business philosophies.Hivos is committed to people in Africa, Asia and Latin America who are systematically blocked from rights, opportunities and resources. A lasting improvement in their situation is the ultimate measure for Hivos work. One of the guiding principles of Hivos philosophy is strengthening the social position of women. Core values of Hivos are: • human dignityand self-determination • pluralism and democracy • focus on material and non-material aspects • mutual solidarity and responsible citizenship • respect for people’s cultural and social identity • responsible management of nature and natural resources
